images.title: Three double number lines
images.purpose: Show the three multipliers side by side: cm over mm (x10), m over cm (x100) and km over m (x1,000), each with the first tick and the example tick.
images.composition: Three stacked pairs of lines, each pair with its arrow and two ticks.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. THREE ROWS, each a pair of horizontal lines 600 px long (x 428 to 1028), the top line the bigger unit and the bottom line the smaller unit 70 px below it, each line with exactly 2 tall ticks (40 px) at x 548 and x 1028. ROW 1 (top line y 150, bottom line y 220): top ticks labelled 1 cm and 6 cm, bottom ticks labelled 10 mm and 60 mm, an arrow on the left with the label ×10 in a teal #0072B2 rounded box 150 by 50 px (x 190 to 340, y 160 to 210). ROW 2 (top line y 380, bottom line y 450): top ticks 1 m and 9 m, bottom ticks 100 cm and 900 cm, the arrow with the label ×100 in an amber #E69F00 box at the same place. ROW 3 (top line y 610, bottom line y 680): top ticks 1 km and 8 km, bottom ticks 1,000 m and 8,000 m, the arrow with the label ×1,000 in a green #009E73 box. All tick labels are 36 px bold, above the top line and below the bottom line. In all: 3 pairs of lines, 12 ticks, 3 arrows. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 3 pairs of lines
images.takeaway: Going down to the smaller unit multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000.
images.description: Three double number lines: cm over mm with ×10, m over cm with ×100 and km over m with ×1,000, each with its example tick.
images.context: Concept image for Changing Between mm, cm, m and km. It follows the idea of the three double number lines in your maths book (cm over mm, m over cm, km over m) and shows the concept's own examples 6 cm, 9 m and 8 km (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Go down each pair with the child. The slip to watch: using ×10 for every pair.
